_readme: Where the official rule sets of VAMPIRE JS and VAMPIRE PHP come from, under which licence their publishers release them, and under which licence the derived rule packages are passed on.

Read by the build of the rule packages ( devkit: import-ruleset.php, export-runtime.php and write-notice.php write the licence into each rule package and generate NOTICE ) and by the builds that pass the rule packages on. This file is the only place where these facts stand.
An entry is found by the FIRST 'match' that occurs in the rule set's source.file ( slashes normalised to '/' ). More specific entries therefore come first.
status 'cleared': the licence allows passing the derived rule package on; the package carries 'packageLicence' as its SPDX identifier, and NOTICE reproduces every file in 'licenceTexts'.

status 'pending': the rights holder states no licence, and the rule set is shipped until the rights holder answers the request that has been made. NOTICE names origin and rights holder and NO licence; 'packageLicence' is NOASSERTION. Such an entry must carry 'separable', so that one build switch can drop it.
status 'open': the licence forbids the form we ship, or no licence is known and nothing was decided; every build STOPS. 'question' says why.

packageLicence: the SPDX identifier written into the head of the derived rule package. The engine files ( vampire.js, src/ of VAMPIRE PHP ) always carry LicenseRef-specialPress-Proprietary; this field never applies to them.

licenceTexts: files under build/licences/ that every package with such a rule set must contain in full. Apache-2.0 section 4(a) and EUPL-1.2 article 5 both require that recipients get a copy of the licence, not a link.
obligations: what a package has to do beyond carrying the licence text, one ASCII sentence each; NOTICE reproduces them.

visibleNotice: a sentence that the user must SEE in the product, not only find in NOTICE ( FeRD's condition for ZUGFeRD ). The rule packages carry it as 'notice', and both engines print it in the report of every check that ran such a rule set. The German text is written with JSON escapes so that this file stays ASCII.

separable: the name of a group that a build switch can drop as a whole ( build-vampire-addon.mjs --without=peppol, export-runtime.php --without=peppol ). Groups in use: peppol, france, cius ( the national CIUS ) and out-of-scope ( Serbia, Turkey, ZATCA ).

The explanation packages and the rule catalogue of einvoice-reference-data read this file too ( build/provenance.php there ): a rule set whose entry is not 'cleared' or 'pending', or which has no entry, is left out of every package and of the rule catalogue instead of stopping that build.

Every statement here was checked against the upstream files or repositories on 2026-10-08, the Factur-X, French and national CIUS entries on 2026-10-09. None of this is legal advice; it stands under the reservation of the legal review that is still recommended.
Keep this file ASCII: NOTICE is plain ASCII, and the builds refuse anything else.

sources.publisher: FNFE-MPE (Forum National de la Facture Electronique et des Marches Publics Electroniques, Paris); authors named in the file header: Quentin Houard and Cyrille Sautereau for FNFE-MPE
sources.licenceStatement: Three statements, read on 2026-10-09. (1) The file header reads 'Schematron derive du schematron EN16931 preprocessed Licensed under European Union Public Licence (EUPL) version 1.4.0'; the second header line says 'based on Schematron EN16931 version 1.3.16'. An EUPL version 1.4.0 does not exist ( the versions are 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 ); the number is the release number of the Schematron, and the CEN source it derives from is EUPL-1.2. (2) The FNFE explanatory note 1.4.0, page 8, in English and French, says that use of the Schematron schemas for standard XP Z12-012 is royalty-free, 'AS IS', and governed by the Apache 2.0 License. (3) The repository fnfempe/France_RFE carries the unmodified Apache License 2.0 as LICENSE ( initial commit 2026-06-10 ). Measured: 841 of 877 assertion identifiers in the CII file and 985 of 1047 in the UBL file are CEN identifiers ( BR-, CII-, UBL- ), only 36 and 62 are French ( BR-FR, BR-FREXT ). The file is therefore mainly EUPL-1.2 material of CEN with FNFE additions under Apache-2.0; the derived rule package is distributed under EUPL-1.2, and both licence texts are included.
sources.copyright: FNFE-MPE for the French additions. The explanatory note carries '(c)2026 FNFE-MPE - All rights reserved' in its page footer; the Schematron files carry no copyright line. The EN 16931 rules restate EN 16931-1:2017, whose copyright is owned by CEN and its members.
sources.upstreamNotice: Schematron derive du schematron EN16931 preprocessed Licensed under European Union Public Licence (EUPL) version 1.4.0. Realise par Quentin Houard et Cyrille Sautereau pour le compte du FNFE-MPE.
obligations: This rule package is a derivative of EUPL-1.2 material and is distributed under EUPL-1.2 only, never under the proprietary licence of the engine.
Apache-2.0 section 4(b): the package states that it is a translation of the FNFE Schematron into the rule format of the engine and not the original file.
Its source form is the rule package itself (readable JSON); the upstream Schematron is published at the address under Source.

One rule set for all French profiles ( EN16931, EXTENDED-CTC-FR, Factur-X BASIC WL, EN16931 and EXTENDED ); the copies in the profile folders are byte-identical ( SHA-256 measured for CII on 2026-10-09 ). sources.publisher: FNFE-MPE (Forum National de la Facture Electronique et des Marches Publics Electroniques, Paris); authors named in the file header: Quentin Houard and Cyrille Sautereau for FNFE-MPE
sources.licenceStatement: Three statements, read on 2026-10-09. (1) The FNFE explanatory note 1.4.0, page 8, in English: 'Use of the Schematron schemas for the XP Z12-012 Standard is royalty-free, on an AS IS basis, subject to the aforementioned limitations, and is governed by the terms of the Apache 2.0 License'; the French note says the same. (2) The repository fnfempe/France_RFE carries the unmodified Apache License 2.0 as LICENSE ( initial commit 2026-06-10 by csautereau ); GitHub reports the SPDX identifier Apache-2.0. (3) Contradicting this, the file header since release 1.4.0 reads 'Schematron Licensed under European Union Public Licence (EUPL) version 1.4.0'. An EUPL version 1.4.0 does not exist ( the versions are 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 ); releases 0.1 to 1.3.1 of the same file carried no licence line at all. Measured: all 170 ( CII ) and 174 ( UBL ) assertion identifiers are French ( BR-FR- ); the file contains no CEN rules. The derived rule package is distributed under EUPL-1.2 with both licence texts, which is permitted under the Apache reading and required under the EUPL reading of the header.

sources.question: No licence statement of eSPap was found in the files or on the site. Not built into any package until eSPap's terms are documented or eSPap is asked.

sources.publisher: AGID ( Agenzia per l'Italia Digitale ) for the Italian rules, OpenPeppol AISBL for the Peppol rules, CEN/TC 434 for the EN 16931 rules; obtained through phive-rules-peppol-italy
sources.copyright: Read on 2026-10-09. The wrapper AGID-EN16931-UBL.sch carries the header of the Peppol wrapper: 'Licensed under European Union Public Licence (EUPL) version 1.2.', 'This schematron uses business terms defined the CEN/EN16931-1 and is reproduced with permission from CEN.' and 'Peppol BIS Billing 3.0.14'. AGID's own files AGID/AGID-EN16931-CIUS-UBL.inc and AGID-EN16931-EXT-UBL.inc carry no licence line, and the package readme says only 'ISO Schematron business rules'. peppol-docs.agid.gov.it and peppol.agid.gov.it state no licence. The legal notes of www.agid.gov.it say 'i dati pubblicati sul presente sito sono messi a disposizione con licenza CC-BY 4.0', which covers that site and not the download site of the Schematron. Measured on the extraction: 1187 rules, 1136 with the origin PEPPOL and 51 NATIONAL; 123 are Italian ( BR-IT ).
sources.upstreamNotice: Licensed under European Union Public Licence (EUPL) version 1.2.
sources.question: Three rights holders in one file. The EUPL line of the wrapper is inherited from the Peppol wrapper and does not grant OpenPeppol's rights; AGID's own rules carry no licence. Not built into any package until the rights are clear.
